newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Tobacco, Cablevision debt up.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Tobacco, Cablevision debt up.

text.p: Reports of an imminent tobacco liability settlement helped tobacco bonds extend their gains, while news regarding Cablevision Systems Corp and Cineplex Odeon Corp drove those bonds higher, traders said.
In the broader U.S. corporate bond markets, prices ended the day largely unchanged on generally sluggish trading activity typical of a summer Friday, traders said.
Bonds of Philip Morris & Cos Inc and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp tightened on Friday morning on reports that a settlement between the tobacco industry and the states would be released in the afternoon.
Analysts said it was difficult to accurately interpret investor reaction to the late-Friday announcement that the tobacco industry had agreed to pay states $368.5 billion over 25 years.

"You will be able to gauge the reaction better when people come in on Monday after digesting the information," said one tobacco industry debt analyst, who was struggling to fully assess the implications of the agreement.
"Spreads were a tad wider on RJR and a unchanged on Philip Morris, but it's Friday at four o'clock and very few people are around," the analyst said.
Initial reports from traders suggested that prices of longer-maturity tobacco bonds were hurt more than those of intermediate-maturity bonds.

Elsewhere, junk bonds of Cablevision Systems jumped one point on Friday on a Wall Street Journal report that News Corp Ltd and Tele-Communications Inc are nearing a deal to buy 40 percent of the Cablevision's sport programming services for around $850 million.
The company's 9 1/4 percent notes of '05 rose to 94 1/4-94/34 from 93-1/4-93-3/4, a trader said. Bonds of News Corp and TCI were unchanged on the news, other traders said.

In other market action, Cineplex Odeon Corp junk bonds rose one point on news that the movie theater company was in discussions with Sony Corp subsidiary Loews Theaters Group regarding a possible merger.
Cineplex 10 7/8 percent notes due '99 were ended the day at 105-106 after closing yesterday at 104-105.
In broader markets, junk bonds drifted higher by 1/8 of a point on low trading volume on Friday, traders said.
In new-issue activity, an EchoStar Communications Corp unit sold $375 million in five-year senior secured notes in a private placement via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette on Friday.
The bonds, rated B2/B-minus, priced to yield 12.50 percent. The deal was increased by $50 million in size.
Also, Equimar Shipholdings Ltd sold $125 million in 10-year first preferred ship mortgage notes in a private placement via Credit Suisse First Boston Corp.
The deal, rated B3/B-plus, priced to yield 9.875 percent and was increased by $75 million in size.
Dealers expected new issue business to continue at its brisk pace, with at least 14 new deals, totalling over $2.5 billion, scheduled to hit the market next week.
In the investment-grade bond market, spreads ended the day unchanged in a slow trading session.
One trader reported a pickup in investor interest in the trust preferred sector at the expense of debt in the Ba3/BBB-minus-ratings sector.
"People are finally coming to their senses. With spread so tight across the board, they are looking to move up in quality while still preserving some yield."
In the government bond market, Treasury prices ended higher as technical buying took the long end of the market to four-month highs before giving way to late-session profit-taking.
The price of the 30-year benchmark Treasury ended 7/32 higher at 99-16/32, pushing its yield down to 6.66 percent.
